_source: bina-gtm/notes/ESA_State_Database.xlsx — the bina team's ESA database. Sync this file from it; never invent numbers or dates. If a field is unknown, use an honest fallback and flag the gap to the team.

programs.who: Any Alabama K–12 family.
programs.applyWindow: One window a year, in spring. Exact 2026 dates aren't published yet — check the CHOOSE Act site, and we'll confirm timing with you.
programs.approval: The state reviews your application after the window closes and confirms your award before funds are released. We'll tell you what to expect for your bina start on the call.

programs.who: Every Arizona K–12 family — no income requirement.
programs.howMuch: $7,000–$8,000 per child, per year (more for children with special needs).
programs.applyWindow: Open all year. Your quarter depends on when you sign — deadlines are Jun 1, Sep 1, Dec 1 and Mar 1. Applying earlier means funds sooner.
programs.approval: Approval takes up to 30 days. You pre-register, then set up ClassWallet and link your bank. Because your funding quarter is set by your contract-signing date, signing with bina early puts you in an earlier funding quarter.
programs.boost: Arizona's handbook explicitly approves “tuition or fees for a nonpublic online learning program” — exactly the category bina is in.

programs.who: Every Arkansas K–12 family.
programs.standing: Our application is with the state and we're waiting on their decision.
programs.applyWindow: Mar 9 – Jun 1, 2026. Finish your application or renewal by Jun 1 to secure your child's place for 2026–27.
programs.approval: Applications are reviewed in priority windows; expect a response about 7–10 business days after you submit your documents. Funds then arrive quarterly through ClassWallet.
programs.soonIntro: Arkansas funds families generously through the EFA, and bina's application is with the state. Here's where we are, and how Arkansas families are joining bina in the meantime.
programs.soonWhy: The Education Freedom Account is open to every Arkansas K–12 family and pays in quarterly installments through ClassWallet — the money is there and moving. What's outstanding is bina's provider status.
programs.soonWork: We've applied and we're chasing a status response from the Arkansas Department of Education. We'll email you the moment it lands.

programs.who: Florida has funded school choice for 25 years, and school choice now reaches more than half of Florida students. If you're a Florida family, the scholarship side is rarely the hard part.
programs.howMuch: Around $8,200 per child each year — more for children with additional needs. That's genuinely close to a full year at bina, which is exactly why we're working to unlock it.
programs.standing: Not yet approved to be paid from these funds — and actively pushing to change that. We'd rather tell you straight than let you find out at the paperwork stage.
programs.applyWindow: Applications open in cycles through the year. You start by contacting Step Up for Students or AAA Scholarship Foundation.
programs.approval: bina isn't a direct Florida provider yet, so today this works through reimbursement — you're funded, then submit bina's invoice, enrollment letter and teacher credentials to claim it. We map your exact path on the call before you spend anything.
programs.soonIntro: Florida is one of the biggest school-choice states in the country — and one we're actively working to open. Here's where we are, and how Florida families are joining bina in the meantime.
programs.soonWhy: Florida's rules are the strictest we've come across: to be paid from the scholarship, a school has to be registered in Florida with a physical campus and Florida curriculum. bina is a global online school without a Florida campus, so we don't fit that box today. Step Up for Students has also confirmed that the PEP scholarship doesn't cover full-time online school, and that reimbursement always comes after you've paid. Florida does fund part-time tutoring — that route needs Florida-licensed tutors, and building that bench is one of the things we're working on.
programs.soonWork: We're calling the Family Empowerment Scholarship program and the Step Up for Students helpdesk directly to get a straight answer on how a school like bina can take part — including whether we can work through a Florida-registered partner. The moment we have it, this page changes and you'll be the first to know.

programs.who: Families under the income limit whose child is zoned for certain public schools.
programs.standing: Not open yet — the state expects certified teachers and asynchronous coursework, which we're working through.
programs.applyWindow: The portal reopens each period. Use the pre-screen tool at mygeorgiapromise.org to check eligibility, then apply.
programs.approval: After the window closes, applications are reviewed — expect about 60 days. Your student's status updates in stages in the portal, so you'll see exactly where you stand before we set your bina start.
programs.soonIntro: Georgia Promise is live for families and bina's application is with the state. Here's where we are, and how Georgia families are joining bina in the meantime.
programs.soonWhy: The Georgia Promise Scholarship is already funding families. Two things stand between bina and that money: Georgia expects teachers certified for the state, and it expects offerings that include asynchronous coursework — bina is built around live, small-group classes.
programs.soonWork: We're chasing our application status with the state and working out internally how to meet the teacher-certification and asynchronous-learning requirements without watering down what bina actually is.

programs.who: Idaho families with a child in nonpublic school (ages 5–19).
programs.howMuch: Up to $5,000 per child, per year ($7,500 for children with special needs).
programs.applyWindow: The second 2026 window opens May 21; apply by Aug 15.
programs.approval: This is a tax credit or advance payment: you apply, submit your bina tuition receipts, and receive a refundable credit or advance payment. We supply the receipts you need.

programs.soonIntro: LA GATOR is one of the strongest programs in the country, but Louisiana ties it to locally licensed tutors. Here's where we are, and how Louisiana families are joining bina in the meantime.
programs.soonWhy: LA GATOR is generous and runs through Odyssey — the same platform bina already works with in approved states. The blocker is Louisiana's requirement that teaching be delivered by Louisiana-licensed tutors, and bina doesn't have Louisiana-licensed teachers on the team today.
programs.soonWork: Our application is drafted and the supporting documents are being collected. The open question is Louisiana licensing for the teachers who'd teach your child — we'd rather solve that properly than get listed and then not be able to deliver.

programs.soonIntro: Texas just launched the biggest school-choice program in the country. Here's exactly where we are with it, and how Texas families are joining bina in the meantime.

noProgramNotes.California: California doesn't have a K–12 ESA or voucher program today. The earliest one could start is the 2027–28 school year, and only if a ballot measure passes in November 2026 — it faces organized opposition, so we're watching it rather than promising it.
